title: A Phase III trial of inhaled mosliciguat in pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease
official: A Phase III, multicenter, randomized, double-blind placebo-controlled trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of inhaled mosliciguat in participants with pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease
summary:
Background and study aims
Pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) is a serious condition where high blood pressure develops in the arteries of the lungs due to underlying inflammation and scarring of lung tissue. The aim of this study is to evaluate whether mosliciguat is better than placebo at improving a participant’s capacity to exercise by Week 24. This will be measured by the 6-minute walk test, which measures the distance a person can walk over 6 minutes. 

Who can participate?
Patients aged 18-85 year with PH-ILD

What does the study involve?
Participants will be randomly allocated to receive mosliciguat or placebo for 24 weeks. Participants who complete the 24-week period may continue to participate in the extension period where all participants receive mosliciguat.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Mosliciguat is still in development, so we cannot predict whether participants will receive a direct benefit from being in this study. However, participation may help other people who have PH-ILD to receive better care in the future and may help determine whether mosliciguat can be part of that care. Study doctors or other members of the study team will explain all risks and discomforts to potential participants. They will also keep careful track of participants’ health during the study to help manage side effects or problems. Participants may leave the study at any time for any reason.

Where is the study run from?
Pulmovant, Inc. (USA)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
August 2026 to August 2029

Who is funding the study?
Pulmovant, Inc. (USA)

Who is the main contact?
Jennifer Cormier, jennifer.cormier@pulmovant.com
conditions: Pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Participants willing and able to provide informed consent
2. Participants with diagnosis of pulmonary hypertension (PH) associated with interstitial lung disease (ILD). Diagnosis will be confirmed by a high resolution computerized tomography (HR-CT) scan showing diffuse parenchymal disease. Eligible diagnosed disease include:
2.1. Idiopathic interstitial pneumonia (IIP)
2.2. Chronic hypersensitivity pneumonitis
2.3. ILD-associated connective tissue disease (CTD) 
3. Confirmed pulmonary hypertension by right heart catheterization (RHC)
4. Ability to perform 6-minute walk distance ≥100 meters
Exclusion criteria:
1. Diagnosis of PH Group 1 (eg, pulmonary arterial hypertension), Group 2 (related to left heart disease), Group 4 (eg, chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension), or Group 5 (eg, unclassified)
2. Exacerbation of underlying lung disease requiring change in therapy or hospitalization within 28 days prior to randomization
3. Receiving >10 l/min oxygen supplementation by any mode of delivery at rest
4. History of intolerance to mosliciguat, or soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC) stimulators or activators
5. Initiation of pulmonary rehabilitation or ongoing acute phase of rehabilitation within 28 days prior to randomization
6. Receipt of investigational or interventional therapy within 42 days OR 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to randomization
